note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace

findings: component-model-async is NOT compiled out of the shipped artifact: wasmtime_config_wasm_component_model_async_set is exported and an engine builds with it enabled (engine_built=true) via the C API.

Only the combination with wasm_stack_switching=True makes engine construction fail, and it fails as a NATIVE ABORT (c-api/src/engine.rs:37 unwrap): 'the wasm_stack_switching feature is not supported on this compiler configuration'.

The Python binding exposes no async call surface at all (no *_async attribute on wasmtime, wasmtime.component, Store, Func, Linker) and Config.wasm_stack_switching has no getter, so the effective posture cannot be read back from the engine.

Under the product configuration the async-lifted shapes behave as measured: malformed shapes are REJECTED at parse; the accepted async-lifted export aborts at component/func.rs:345 ('async-lifted exports should have failed validation when component-model-async feature disabled') at CALL time, i.e. BEFORE any host->guest callback trampoline runs; no leg returned a value.
On native Linux the same abort is contained by the worker boundary (worker_crash_asynclift: exit 1, parent_survived=true) — see native_linux/09_protected_runs.jsonl.
isolation: every leg in its own child interpreter; a native abort IS the measurement, not a harness failure
recommended_architecture_step_not_implem: pre-validate every component with wasmparser >= 1.260.0 (or an equivalent reject-async gate) before handing bytes to Wasmtime, so the refusal is a clean up-front validation error instead of an engine abort. NOT implemented in this verification round: no new runtime features are authorised.

vendor_preconditions.source: GHSA description (bytecodealliance/wasmtime repo advisory, state=published, severity=critical)
vendor_preconditions.summary: async-lifted callback result count is unvalidated -> guest writes up to ~16KB of chosen data onto the native stack (return-address overwrite)
vendor_preconditions.vendor_workaround: disable the component-model-async feature (Wasmtime then rejects components using async features), or pre-validate with wasmparser >= 1.260.0

verdict.classification: REACHABLE FOR THE ARTIFACT / NOT REACHED UNDER THE DEPLOYED PROFILE — the pilot claim must be stated this way, not as 'unreachable'.
verdict.critical_path_under_deployed_configurati: NOT EXECUTED (measured, not inferred from missing methods)
verdict.protection_level: deployment invariant + process wall, NOT an artifact-level guarantee
residual_risk: R1: any embedder that links the same _libwasmtime and enables component-model-async through the C API can reach the async runtime; 49.0.0 keeps the unvalidated callback result count, so the overflow is reachable for such an embedder.
R2: the guard is the engine's own call-time abort, which is a PROCESS ABORT rather than a clean validation error; a worker that aborts is contained, but the abort is the mechanism.
R3: the posture is not attestable by read-back (no getter for wasm_stack_switching); the signed security_baseline field is a host-side constant, so it documents intent, not engine state.
R4: no 49.0.2 wheel exists yet, so the vendor fix is not installable (check_wasmtime_patch.py, 2026-10-13).
